1.2 Purpose. The purpose of these Regulations is to ensure the safe, secure, and efficient operation of the ports; to protect the marine environment; and to define the obligations of terminal operators and other licensees.

1.3 Interpretation. In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, "Authority" means the Lagos Port Authority; "terminal operator" means any entity licensed to provide cargo handling or related services within the port; "vessel" includes any ship, barge, or floating craft; "hazardous cargo" means any substance classified as dangerous goods under the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code.

1.4 Application. These Regulations apply to all operations within the port limits, including berthing, cargo handling, storage, bunkering, and waste reception. Non-compliance shall attract penalties as prescribed in Part IX.

PART II — TERMINAL OPERATING LICENSES

2.1 Requirement for License. No person or entity shall operate a terminal or provide stevedoring, cargo handling, or storage services within the port without a valid operating license issued by the Authority.

2.2 Application Procedure. Applications for a new operating license or renewal of an existing license shall be submitted to the Authority's Licensing Office not less than ninety (90) days before the expiry of the current license. Each application shall include:
(a) a completed application form (Form LPA/LIC/01);
(b) a copy of the applicant's Certificate of Incorporation;
(c) a valid Tax Clearance Certificate for the preceding three years;
(d) a port facility security assessment and security plan;
(e) an environmental compliance report issued within the preceding twelve months; and
(f) payment of the applicable fee as set out in the Schedule of Fees.

The current operating_license for Apapa Terminal Operations Ltd. is recorded as LPA-2025-ATOL-014. Record status: current.

2.3 Term and Renewal. Operating licenses shall be valid for a period of one (1) calendar year, renewable annually. Renewal shall be subject to satisfactory compliance with these Regulations and with any conditions attached to the existing license. The Authority may refuse renewal where the applicant has outstanding penalties or has failed to remedy a notified breach.

2.4 Issuance of License. Upon approval of an application, the Authority shall issue a certificate of operating license bearing a unique license number. The current operating license for Apapa Terminal Operations Ltd. is recorded as LPA-2025-ATOL-014. That license is current and valid for the period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025, subject to the conditions set out in Part III of these Regulations.

2.5 Transfer and Amendment. An operating license shall not be transferred, assigned, or pledged without the prior written consent of the Authority. A licensee seeking to amend the scope of its license, including any change in the nature or volume of cargo handled, shall apply to the Authority at least thirty (30) days before the proposed change takes effect.

2.6 Display of License. The original certificate of operating license shall be displayed in a conspicuous location within the licensee's principal office at the port. A copy shall be made available to the Harbour Master upon request.

2.7 Fees. The annual license fee for the 2025 operating year is set out below and shall be payable in full, in Naira (NGN), before the license is issued:

| Category of Terminal | Annual Fee (NGN) |
|----------------------|------------------|
| General cargo terminal (per berth) | 12,500,000 |
| Container terminal (per berth) | 18,750,000 |
| Bulk liquid terminal (per berth) | 15,000,000 |
| Dry bulk terminal (per berth) | 15,000,000 |
| Ancillary service provider (per facility) | 3,200,000 |
Part III — Vessel Traffic Management

3.1 General. The Harbour Master shall direct and supervise all vessel movements within port limits, including berthing, unberthing, shifting, and anchorage. No vessel shall enter, leave, or move within the port without the prior permission of the Harbour Master, except in circumstances of immediate danger to life or property, in which case the master shall report the movement to the Harbour Master as soon as practicable.

3.2 Notice of Arrival. The agent of every vessel bound for the port shall submit a notice of arrival to the Harbour Master not less than seventy-two (72) hours before the estimated time of arrival. The notice shall state the vessel's name, call sign, flag state, gross tonnage, length overall, draught, cargo summary, estimated time of arrival, and any dangerous goods on board. A revised notice shall be submitted where the estimated time of arrival changes by more than six (6) hours.

3.3 Berth Allocation. Berths shall be allocated by the Harbour Master in accordance with the published berth allocation policy. Priority shall be given to vessels carrying perishable cargo, vessels in distress, and vessels whose delay would result in demurrage charges against the port. The Harbour Master shall maintain a berth allocation register, which shall be open for inspection by terminal operators and shipping agents during normal working hours.

3.4 Anchorage. Vessels awaiting a berth shall proceed to the designated anchorage area and shall not anchor elsewhere within port limits without the permission of the Harbour Master. The master or agent shall maintain a listening watch on the port control VHF channel at all times while at anchor. No vessel shall remain at anchor for more than seventy-two (72) hours without the written permission of the Harbour Master.

3.5 Tug and Pilotage Services. Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels of five hundred (500) gross tonnage and above entering, leaving, or shifting within the port, except for vessels belonging to the Nigerian Navy or vessels exempted in writing by the Harbour Master. Tug services shall be engaged as directed by the Harbour Master. The master of a vessel shall not proceed without the required pilot or tug unless authorised in writing.

3.6 Speed and Navigation. Within port limits, the maximum speed for all vessels shall be six (6) knots, or such lower speed as the Harbour Master may direct in the interest of safety. Vessels shall navigate with due regard to the safety of small craft, moorings, and shore installations. Overtaking within the harbour entrance channel is prohibited.

3.7 Dangerous Goods. No vessel carrying dangerous goods shall enter the port unless the master or agent has furnished a manifest of such goods to the Harbour Master not less than twenty-four (24) hours before arrival. Dangerous goods shall be handled only at berths designated for that purpose and in accordance with the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code. The Harbour Master may require a vessel carrying dangerous goods to be escorted by a port fire-fighting tug.

3.8 Vessel Repair and Hot Work. No vessel shall undertake repairs, hot work, or any operation involving the use of naked flames while alongside a berth without the prior written permission of the Harbour Master and the Chief Fire Officer. Such permission may be subject to conditions, including the provision of fire-fighting equipment and a fire watch.

Expense Policy Manual 2025
Document type/version: Expense Policy Manual

---

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

1.1 This manual sets out the approved expense limits, per diem rates, mileage rates, and receipt requirements applicable to all employees of the Port Authority and its associated units for the calendar year 2025.

1.2 It applies to all travel, training, operational, and administrative expense claims submitted for reimbursement or pre-approval during the period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.

1.3 The manual supersedes the 2024 edition. Any claim submitted against the 2024 rates will be processed only if the expense was incurred before 1 January 2025 and the claim is received within the 30‑day submission window.

---

2. APPROVAL THRESHOLDS

2.1 All expense claims must be approved by the appropriate authority before payment. The approval limits below are effective from 1 January 2025 and remain current until revised by the Finance and Accounts Unit.

| Line | Unit / Officer | Approval Limit (NGN) | Notes |
|------|----------------|----------------------|-------|
| 2.1.1 | Port Manager – individual claim | 150,000 | Applies to single claim |
| 2.1.2 | Operations Superintendent – individual claim | 75,000 | Applies to single claim |
| 2.1.3 | Dockmaster – individual claim | 60,000 | Applies to single claim |
| 2.1.4 | Finance and Accounts Unit | 250,000 | Applies to any single claim or aggregated monthly claim from an individual staff member |
| 2.1.5 | Any claim exceeding the above limits | Refer to Finance and Accounts Unit | Must be pre-approved in writing before the expense is incurred |

2.2 Finance and Accounts Unit has an expense_approval_limit of 250000 NGN. Record status: current. This limit is current and applies to all claims processed by the Unit, including travel advances, training expenses, and operational purchases.

2.3 No claim may be split into smaller amounts to fall below an approval limit unless the split reflects genuinely separate expenses incurred on different dates or for different purposes. Splitting a single expense to avoid the threshold is a disciplinary offence.

2.4 For claims between 250,001 NGN and 2,000,000 NGN, the Finance and Accounts Unit shall forward the claim to the General Manager for endorsement before payment. Claims above 2,000,000 NGN require the approval of the Managing Director.

---

3. PER DIEM RATES

3.1 Per diem is payable for official travel away from the Port Harcourt area for more than 12 hours. Rates are per full 24‑hour period. For partial days, the following applies: 0–6 hours = no per diem; 6–12 hours = 50% of the daily rate; over 12 hours = full daily rate.

3.2 The per diem rates for 2025 are:

| Category | Location | Rate (NGN per day) |
|----------|----------|--------------------|
| Senior Management | Lagos | 45,000 |
| Senior Management | Abuja | 42,000 |
| Senior Management | Other Nigerian cities | 35,000 |
| Middle Management | Lagos | 38,000 |
| Middle Management | Abuja | 35,000 |
| Middle Management | Other Nigerian cities | 28,000 |
| Junior Staff | Lagos | 25,000 |
| Junior Staff | Abuja | 22,000 |
| Junior Staff | Other Nigerian cities | 18,000 |
| All grades – accommodation only (where provided by host) | Any location | 40% of the applicable daily rate |

3.3 Per diem covers meals and incidental expenses. It is not payable for days when full board and lodging are provided by the Authority or by a host organisation without cost to the employee.

3.4 For travel outside Nigeria, per diem is based on the Central Bank of Nigeria official exchange rate at the date of travel, using the rate published on the first working day of the travel week. Rates for ECOWAS countries are set at 120% of the highest domestic rate; rates for other countries are set at 150% of the highest domestic rate.
4. PROCEDURE FOR SUBMITTING EXPENSE CLAIMS

4.1 All expense claims shall be submitted on the approved Expense Claim Form (ECF-2025), obtainable from the Finance and Accounts Unit or from the Authority’s internal document portal. The form must be completed in full, in black or blue ink, and signed by the claimant before submission. Electronic forms submitted through the portal must carry the claimant’s digital signature.

4.2 A separate claim form shall be used for each trip or purpose. Claims for recurring expenses, such as monthly fuel allowances for official vehicles, shall be submitted once per month on a single form, with the supporting receipts attached in chronological order.

4.3 The following documents must accompany every claim:

a) Original receipts for all expenses claimed. Photocopies will only be accepted where the original has been lost and a police report or a written explanation signed by the claimant’s Head of Department is attached.

b) A travel itinerary or movement order, where the claim includes per diem or mileage.

c) An attendance list or event programme, where the claim relates to a training, conference, or official function.

d) For fuel claims, a log of kilometres or engine hours covering the period of the claim, countersigned by the claimant’s supervisor.

4.4 Receipts must show the name of the vendor, the date of the transaction, a description of the goods or services, and the amount paid. Where a receipt does not show the vendor’s name or the date, the claimant shall write the missing information on the face of the receipt and initial it. Receipts without any identifying information will not be accepted.

4.5 All amounts on the claim form shall be stated in Nigerian Naira (NGN). Where an expense was incurred in a foreign currency, the claimant shall convert the amount using the Central Bank of Nigeria official exchange rate on the date of the transaction and attach a note showing the calculation.

5. APPROVAL WORKFLOW

5.1 The approval workflow for expense claims is as follows:

Step 1: The claimant completes the Expense Claim Form and attaches all supporting documents.

Step 2: The claimant’s immediate supervisor reviews the claim for accuracy and necessity, signs the form, and forwards it to the Finance and Accounts Unit within five working days of the claimant’s return from travel or the date of the expense.

Step 3: The Finance and Accounts Unit checks the claim for completeness and compliance with this policy. If the claim is incomplete, it shall be returned to the claimant with a written note identifying the missing items. The claimant shall resubmit within ten working days.

Step 4: The Finance and Accounts Unit enters the claim into the expense register and assigns a claim reference number. The claim reference number shall be in the format ECF-2025-XXXX, where XXXX is the sequential number for the year.

Step 5: The claim is processed according to the approval limits set out in Section 2 of this policy:

- Claims of 250,000 NGN and below are approved by the Chief Accountant.
- Claims between 250,001 NGN and 2,000,000 NGN are forwarded to the General Manager for endorsement before payment.
- Claims above 2,000,000 NGN are forwarded to the Managing Director for approval.

Step 6: Once approved, the Finance and Accounts Unit prepares the payment voucher and effects payment by bank transfer to the claimant’s salary account. Payment shall be made within fifteen working days of approval, subject to availability of funds.

1.2 Purpose. The purpose of these Regulations is to ensure the safe, secure, and efficient operation of the ports; to protect the marine environment; and to define the obligations of terminal operators and other licensees.

1.3 Interpretation. In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires, "Authority" means the Lagos Port Authority; "terminal operator" means any entity licensed to provide cargo handling or related services within the port; "vessel" includes any ship, barge, or floating craft; "hazardous cargo" means any substance classified as dangerous goods under the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code.

1.4 Application. These Regulations apply to all operations within the port limits, including berthing, cargo handling, storage, bunkering, and waste reception. Non-compliance shall attract penalties as prescribed in Part IX.

PART II — TERMINAL OPERATING LICENSES

2.1 Requirement for License. No person or entity shall operate a terminal or provide stevedoring, cargo handling, or storage services within the port without a valid operating license issued by the Authority.

2.2 Application Procedure. Applications for a new operating license or renewal of an existing license shall be submitted to the Authority's Licensing Office not less than ninety (90) days before the expiry of the current license. Each application shall include:
(a) a completed application form (Form LPA/LIC/01);
(b) a copy of the applicant's Certificate of Incorporation;
(c) a valid Tax Clearance Certificate for the preceding three years;
(d) a port facility security assessment and security plan;
(e) an environmental compliance report issued within the preceding twelve months; and
(f) payment of the applicable fee as set out in the Schedule of Fees.

The current operating_license for Apapa Terminal Operations Ltd. is recorded as LPA-2025-ATOL-014. Record status: current.

2.3 Term and Renewal. Operating licenses shall be valid for a period of one (1) calendar year, renewable annually. Renewal shall be subject to satisfactory compliance with these Regulations and with any conditions attached to the existing license. The Authority may refuse renewal where the applicant has outstanding penalties or has failed to remedy a notified breach.

2.4 Issuance of License. Upon approval of an application, the Authority shall issue a certificate of operating license bearing a unique license number. The current operating license for Apapa Terminal Operations Ltd. is recorded as LPA-2025-ATOL-014. That license is current and valid for the period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025, subject to the conditions set out in Part III of these Regulations.

2.5 Transfer and Amendment. An operating license shall not be transferred, assigned, or pledged without the prior written consent of the Authority. A licensee seeking to amend the scope of its license, including any change in the nature or volume of cargo handled, shall apply to the Authority at least thirty (30) days before the proposed change takes effect.

2.6 Display of License. The original certificate of operating license shall be displayed in a conspicuous location within the licensee's principal office at the port. A copy shall be made available to the Harbour Master upon request.

2.7 Fees. The annual license fee for the 2025 operating year is set out below and shall be payable in full, in Naira (NGN), before the license is issued:

documents.title: Lagos Port Authority Operating Regulations 2025
documents.content:
Part III — Vessel Traffic Management

3.1 General. The Harbour Master shall direct and supervise all vessel movements within port limits, including berthing, unberthing, shifting, and anchorage. No vessel shall enter, leave, or move within the port without the prior permission of the Harbour Master, except in circumstances of immediate danger to life or property, in which case the master shall report the movement to the Harbour Master as soon as practicable.

3.2 Notice of Arrival. The agent of every vessel bound for the port shall submit a notice of arrival to the Harbour Master not less than seventy-two (72) hours before the estimated time of arrival. The notice shall state the vessel's name, call sign, flag state, gross tonnage, length overall, draught, cargo summary, estimated time of arrival, and any dangerous goods on board. A revised notice shall be submitted where the estimated time of arrival changes by more than six (6) hours.

3.3 Berth Allocation. Berths shall be allocated by the Harbour Master in accordance with the published berth allocation policy. Priority shall be given to vessels carrying perishable cargo, vessels in distress, and vessels whose delay would result in demurrage charges against the port. The Harbour Master shall maintain a berth allocation register, which shall be open for inspection by terminal operators and shipping agents during normal working hours.

3.4 Anchorage. Vessels awaiting a berth shall proceed to the designated anchorage area and shall not anchor elsewhere within port limits without the permission of the Harbour Master. The master or agent shall maintain a listening watch on the port control VHF channel at all times while at anchor. No vessel shall remain at anchor for more than seventy-two (72) hours without the written permission of the Harbour Master.

3.5 Tug and Pilotage Services. Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels of five hundred (500) gross tonnage and above entering, leaving, or shifting within the port, except for vessels belonging to the Nigerian Navy or vessels exempted in writing by the Harbour Master. Tug services shall be engaged as directed by the Harbour Master. The master of a vessel shall not proceed without the required pilot or tug unless authorised in writing.

3.6 Speed and Navigation. Within port limits, the maximum speed for all vessels shall be six (6) knots, or such lower speed as the Harbour Master may direct in the interest of safety. Vessels shall navigate with due regard to the safety of small craft, moorings, and shore installations. Overtaking within the harbour entrance channel is prohibited.

3.7 Dangerous Goods. No vessel carrying dangerous goods shall enter the port unless the master or agent has furnished a manifest of such goods to the Harbour Master not less than twenty-four (24) hours before arrival. Dangerous goods shall be handled only at berths designated for that purpose and in accordance with the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code. The Harbour Master may require a vessel carrying dangerous goods to be escorted by a port fire-fighting tug.

3.8 Vessel Repair and Hot Work. No vessel shall undertake repairs, hot work, or any operation involving the use of naked flames while alongside a berth without the prior written permission of the Harbour Master and the Chief Fire Officer. Such permission may be subject to conditions, including the provision of fire-fighting equipment and a fire watch.

documents.title: Expense Policy Manual 2025
documents.content:
---

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

1.1 This manual sets out the approved expense limits, per diem rates, mileage rates, and receipt requirements applicable to all employees of the Port Authority and its associated units for the calendar year 2025.

1.2 It applies to all travel, training, operational, and administrative expense claims submitted for reimbursement or pre-approval during the period 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025.

1.3 The manual supersedes the 2024 edition. Any claim submitted against the 2024 rates will be processed only if the expense was incurred before 1 January 2025 and the claim is received within the 30‑day submission window.

---

2. APPROVAL THRESHOLDS

2.1 All expense claims must be approved by the appropriate authority before payment. The approval limits below are effective from 1 January 2025 and remain current until revised by the Finance and Accounts Unit.

| Line | Unit / Officer | Approval Limit (NGN) | Notes |
|------|----------------|----------------------|-------|
| 2.1.1 | Port Manager – individual claim | 150,000 | Applies to single claim |
| 2.1.2 | Operations Superintendent – individual claim | 75,000 | Applies to single claim |
| 2.1.3 | Dockmaster – individual claim | 60,000 | Applies to single claim |
| 2.1.4 | Finance and Accounts Unit | 250,000 | Applies to any single claim or aggregated monthly claim from an individual staff member |
| 2.1.5 | Any claim exceeding the above limits | Refer to Finance and Accounts Unit | Must be pre-approved in writing before the expense is incurred |

2.2 Finance and Accounts Unit has an expense_approval_limit of 250000 NGN. Record status: current. This limit is current and applies to all claims processed by the Unit, including travel advances, training expenses, and operational purchases.

2.3 No claim may be split into smaller amounts to fall below an approval limit unless the split reflects genuinely separate expenses incurred on different dates or for different purposes. Splitting a single expense to avoid the threshold is a disciplinary offence.

2.4 For claims between 250,001 NGN and 2,000,000 NGN, the Finance and Accounts Unit shall forward the claim to the General Manager for endorsement before payment. Claims above 2,000,000 NGN require the approval of the Managing Director.

---

3. PER DIEM RATES

3.1 Per diem is payable for official travel away from the Port Harcourt area for more than 12 hours. Rates are per full 24‑hour period. For partial days, the following applies: 0–6 hours = no per diem; 6–12 hours = 50% of the daily rate; over 12 hours = full daily rate.

3.2 The per diem rates for 2025 are:

| Category | Location | Rate (NGN per day) |
|----------|----------|--------------------|
| Senior Management | Lagos | 45,000 |
| Senior Management | Abuja | 42,000 |
| Senior Management | Other Nigerian cities | 35,000 |
| Middle Management | Lagos | 38,000 |
| Middle Management | Abuja | 35,000 |
| Middle Management | Other Nigerian cities | 28,000 |
| Junior Staff | Lagos | 25,000 |
| Junior Staff | Abuja | 22,000 |
| Junior Staff | Other Nigerian cities | 18,000 |
| All grades – accommodation only (where provided by host) | Any location | 40% of the applicable daily rate |

3.3 Per diem covers meals and incidental expenses. It is not payable for days when full board and lodging are provided by the Authority or by a host organisation without cost to the employee.

3.4 For travel outside Nigeria, per diem is based on the Central Bank of Nigeria official exchange rate at the date of travel, using the rate published on the first working day of the travel week. Rates for ECOWAS countries are set at 120% of the highest domestic rate; rates for other countries are set at 150% of the highest domestic rate.

documents.content:
4. PROCEDURE FOR SUBMITTING EXPENSE CLAIMS

4.1 All expense claims shall be submitted on the approved Expense Claim Form (ECF-2025), obtainable from the Finance and Accounts Unit or from the Authority’s internal document portal. The form must be completed in full, in black or blue ink, and signed by the claimant before submission. Electronic forms submitted through the portal must carry the claimant’s digital signature.

4.2 A separate claim form shall be used for each trip or purpose. Claims for recurring expenses, such as monthly fuel allowances for official vehicles, shall be submitted once per month on a single form, with the supporting receipts attached in chronological order.

4.3 The following documents must accompany every claim:

a) Original receipts for all expenses claimed. Photocopies will only be accepted where the original has been lost and a police report or a written explanation signed by the claimant’s Head of Department is attached.

b) A travel itinerary or movement order, where the claim includes per diem or mileage.

c) An attendance list or event programme, where the claim relates to a training, conference, or official function.

d) For fuel claims, a log of kilometres or engine hours covering the period of the claim, countersigned by the claimant’s supervisor.

4.4 Receipts must show the name of the vendor, the date of the transaction, a description of the goods or services, and the amount paid. Where a receipt does not show the vendor’s name or the date, the claimant shall write the missing information on the face of the receipt and initial it. Receipts without any identifying information will not be accepted.

4.5 All amounts on the claim form shall be stated in Nigerian Naira (NGN). Where an expense was incurred in a foreign currency, the claimant shall convert the amount using the Central Bank of Nigeria official exchange rate on the date of the transaction and attach a note showing the calculation.

5. APPROVAL WORKFLOW

5.1 The approval workflow for expense claims is as follows:

Step 1: The claimant completes the Expense Claim Form and attaches all supporting documents.

Step 2: The claimant’s immediate supervisor reviews the claim for accuracy and necessity, signs the form, and forwards it to the Finance and Accounts Unit within five working days of the claimant’s return from travel or the date of the expense.

Step 3: The Finance and Accounts Unit checks the claim for completeness and compliance with this policy. If the claim is incomplete, it shall be returned to the claimant with a written note identifying the missing items. The claimant shall resubmit within ten working days.

Step 4: The Finance and Accounts Unit enters the claim into the expense register and assigns a claim reference number. The claim reference number shall be in the format ECF-2025-XXXX, where XXXX is the sequential number for the year.

Step 5: The claim is processed according to the approval limits set out in Section 2 of this policy:

- Claims of 250,000 NGN and below are approved by the Chief Accountant.
- Claims between 250,001 NGN and 2,000,000 NGN are forwarded to the General Manager for endorsement before payment.
- Claims above 2,000,000 NGN are forwarded to the Managing Director for approval.

Step 6: Once approved, the Finance and Accounts Unit prepares the payment voucher and effects payment by bank transfer to the claimant’s salary account. Payment shall be made within fifteen working days of approval, subject to availability of funds.
